newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba sugar cane harvest at 2 mln tonnes - official.
newsitem.headline: Cuba sugar cane harvest at 2 mln tonnes - official.

text.p: Cuba has harvested about two million tonnes of sugar cane so far this season, Vice President Carlos Lage said on Wednesday.
Lage, speaking to reporters after attending a conference on the economy, said in reply to a question that the harvest was "more or less" at two million tonnes.
He said the harvest, which began in December, was currently at its "decisive moment" when milling was at its peak.

Lage said the 1996-97 harvest had begun late, largely because of delays in foreign financing, which he attributed to the year-old U.S. Helms-Burton Act. He said the measure, which seeks to curb foreign investment in Cuba, initially interrupted foreign financing.

Lage said another difficulty faced by Cuba in the current harvest was dry weather during the past summer, as well as damage in some areas from Hurricane Lili, which swept across parts of the country in October.
Lage repeated the official view that Cuba would show only a "modest" increase in sugar cane production in 1996-97, though he did not give a target figure.
Even though only a small increase was foreseen, Lage said the harvest was expected to be more efficient, requiring fewer resources and costing less.

Some experts have estimated an increase of only a few hundred thousand tonnes over the previous harvest of 4.5 million tonnes. The 1995-96 harvest marked a halt in a disastrous slide in production that began the early 1990s.
Authorities last month said the island nation had produced its first one million tonnes by February 10, after 70 days of harvesting.
